skill.name: agent-memory-systems
skill.description: Design agent memory systems with short-term context, long-term vector storage, and retrieval patterns for semantic, episodic, and procedural memory.
skill.summary: Guide agents to design, retrieve, test, and maintain durable memory systems.

content.value_statement: Agents lose useful context when memory is unstructured. This skill guides memory types, vector storage, retrieval, decay, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains semantic, episodic, and procedural memory using the CoALA framework.
Compares Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, ChromaDB, and pgvector for memory storage.
Shows retrieval patterns with filtering, metadata, hybrid search, and reranking.
Covers chunking, embedding model choice, memory decay, and production testing.
Lists failure modes such as stale memories, missing filters, and untested chunk sizes.
Defines when to involve data, machine learning, knowledge graph, and RAG specialists.
limitations: The skill is a markdown guide and does not install or configure databases.
Code examples require adaptation before use in a production application.
It does not benchmark retrieval quality for a specific dataset or workload.
It assumes the user can choose and operate their own storage provider.

use_cases.title: Plan Persistent Agent Memory
use_cases.description: Design memory layers for an agent that must remember users, tasks, and outcomes across sessions.

use_cases.title: Add Personalization Safely
use_cases.description: Create user-scoped memory retrieval that keeps preferences separate and avoids cross-user leakage.

use_cases.title: Select a Vector Store
use_cases.description: Compare storage options by scale, filtering, hybrid search, latency, and operational complexity.

prompt_templates.title: Map Memory Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to classify my agent data into semantic, episodic, and procedural memory. Explain what should be stored and why.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Storage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to recommend a vector store for my agent memory system. Consider scale, filtering, hybrid search, cost, and operations.

prompt_templates.title: Design Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a retrieval flow for user-scoped memory. Include metadata filters, ranking, decay, and evaluation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Memory Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my memory architecture for leakage risks, stale memory, missing metadata, weak chunking, and poor retrieval tests.

output_examples.input: I need memory for a customer support agent that remembers users across sessions.
output: Use semantic memory for stable user preferences and account facts.
Use episodic memory for past support interactions and resolved issues.
Require user filters on every retrieval to prevent cross-account leakage.

output_examples.input: Which vector store should I use for a small prototype with local development?
output_examples.output: ChromaDB or pgvector fits a small prototype. Choose pgvector if PostgreSQL is already part of the stack.

output_examples.input: My memory search returns irrelevant old facts.
output: Add recency-aware ranking and decay rules.
Test chunk sizes against real queries.
Rerank initial candidates before adding them to the agent context.

best_practices: Filter every memory query by user or tenant before ranking results.
Measure retrieval accuracy with real tasks before production release.
Store metadata such as user, type, timestamp, source, and confidence with each memory.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on semantic similarity alone for private user memory.
Do not keep old memories forever without decay or conflict handling.
Do not choose chunk sizes without testing retrieval quality.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps design agent memory systems that retrieve useful context across sessions.

faq.question: Does it create a working memory database?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples that users adapt to their stack.

faq.question: Which tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It covers LangMem, MemGPT, Letta, Mem0, Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, ChromaDB, and pgvector.

faq.question: Can it help prevent memory data leaks?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes metadata filters, user scoping, and checks for unsafe vector queries.

faq.question: Is it useful for RAG systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers chunking, embeddings, retrieval, hybrid search, and reranking patterns.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: AI engineers, product engineers, and platform architects who build agents with persistent memory.
